name: Siddhartha Gautama
role: Historical Buddha and primary founding teacher of Buddhism
name_note: Siddhartha is the Sanskrit personal name; Gautama (Pali: Gotama) identifies the clan lineage. Shakyamuni means 'Sage of the Shakya clan'.
period: commonly placed in the 5th century BCE; exact dates remain debated
life_summary: According to early Buddhist traditions, Siddhartha Gautama left household life as a young adult, pursued liberation through study, meditation and ascetic practice, rejected extremes, awakened under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya, and spent the remainder of his life teaching the Dharma and establishing the Sangha.
historical_method: The repository separates historical claims from Buddhist traditional biography. Exact dates and details of the Buddha's life are uncertain; early Buddhist texts do not provide a single continuous biography, and later biographies contain substantial legendary material.
source_notes: Early Buddhist textual traditions preserve teachings and episodes rather than one contemporary continuous biography.
Modern scholarship generally places the Buddha in the 5th century BCE, while traditional chronologies can give earlier dates.
